evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 10.58 mg/L at 47.8 h falling to 3.28 mg/L at 51.8 h (rows time_h 478-518 of receiving observations)
Recent 4-h decline rate ~0.30 mg/L/h; linear fit 48-52 h gives -0.248 mg/L/h and ~4-5 h to the 2 mg/L limit under KEEP
Source batches held DO ~9-13 mg/L at comparable times (e.g. source-1 9.4-10.5 mg/L, source-3 10-10.5 mg/L near 48 h), confirming a receiving-specific oxygen deficit
Receiving delayed assays: P = 2.98 g/L at 47.9 h (latest), rising from 1.12 g/L at 35.8 h — product mass worth retaining but secondary to DO constraint
Allowed action bounds: combined = (0.8 feed, 1.15 air), a dual demand/supply correction larger than increase_air alone
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~10.6 mg/L at 48 h to 3.28 mg/L at 52 h (~-0.30 mg/L/h recent slope), far below all source batches at comparable times, and KEEP extrapolates to breach the 2 mg/L hard limit in ~4-5 h. The combined action (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) both cuts oxygen demand ~20% and raises transfer ~15%, matching the observed deficit from both sides, while retaining more product mass than strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed) given P is only beginning to accumulate (latest assay 2.98 g/L). increase_air or reduce_feed alone each leave one side of the balance unaddressed; stop is not warranted when a bounded dual-lever intervention is supported by the evidence.
args.uncertainty: Hidden OUR kinetics, true aeration headroom, and model mismatch mean feasible DO >= 2 mg/L under combined cannot be guaranteed; the projection to breach under KEEP is an extrapolation of a ~4 h sensor trend and could over/understate the deficit. If DO keeps falling post-intervention, escalation (strong_feed_reduction or stop) is the documented fallback. No physical safety is established; this is a simulated recommendation only.
